levushei_serad.en: Per the explanation of R' Chaim. R' Chaim holds the reason for shenayim mikra ve'echad targum is so one will be familiar with what the congregation reads; and if so, likewise for the Festival portion. But the other poskim hold the reason is shnayim mikra ve'echad targum so that each person of Israel reads the entire Torah for himself from beginning to end. And for this reason he ruled in Shulchan Aruch that one need not read the Festival portion — because Magen Avraham s.k. 10 wrote; and per this view what is practiced in reading the haftarah as Rama wrote is also so one completes each year with the congregation every Shabbat what they read — if so, even with many weddings one must read what the congregation reads. And Magen Avraham resolved: the reason of shnayim mikra ve'echad targum for the other poskim does not apply to haftarah at all; and the poskim agree the custom of haftarah is for the reason of R' Chaim lest they call him for maftir and he not be familiar. And that they needed shnayim mikra ve'echad targum for their reason is because in the reading there is no reason of R' Chaim since the chazzan reads:

magen_avraham.he:

magen_avraham.en:
(1) OT to happen 20. He has already recited the whole turn from the day of Shabbat on his Shabbat [15] and on the eve of Shatt he will recite and this is the blessing [Konot]:

And it requires study — for this is per the explanation of R' Chaim; and according to my view he must repeat parashat Yitro to be accustomed to what the congregation reads, as Tosefta writes siman 23; and the Rabbeynu already ruled one need not repeat parashat Yitro; and it must be said that nevertheless the haftarah must be repeated for this because he himself is maftir, unlike in the reading where the chazzan reads as above; and in Levush he omitted this gloss that requires study — for if he never repeats, perhaps Shushan Ashish haftarah will be read for him and he will not be accustomed to it as siman 139 writes; therefore it appears to me he should repeat it; but if there are many weddings one after another he need not again; and it implies in four parshiyot it is obvious he reads the haftarah of the four parshiyot; and in Kenesset HaGedolah he wrote his custom to repeat the haftarah of the sidra and I did not know the reason:

(ג) (כ) Of Shabbat and not, etc. — meaning there is a custom in some places that the congregation reads alone the haftarah of the sedra plus some verses from the haftarah of 'Ashishis yasis chasan' [because it is written therein 'Like a groom adorning a crown,' etc.], and it teaches that when one reads for himself the haftarah he need not read these verses because it is common and fluent in everyone's mouth and he is familiar with them without this reading.
